questions.prompt: An object displaces \(3.0\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m^3}\) of water. Find the buoyant force.
A buoyant force of \(12\,\mathrm{N}\) acts on an object in oil of density \(800\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\). Find the displaced volume.
A body weighs \(45\,\mathrm{N}\) in air and displaces \(2.5\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3}\) of water when fully immersed. Find the supporting force reading while it is immersed.
questions.answer:
The buoyant force is
\[
F_B=(1000)(9.8)(2.5\times10^{-3})=24.5\,\mathrm{N}
\]
The support reading is
\[
N=W-F_B=45-24.5=20.5\,\mathrm{N}
\]

questions.prompt: A uniform object of density \(600\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\) floats in water. What fraction of its volume is submerged?
questions.answer:
For a floating uniform object,
\[
\rho_f gV_{\mathrm{sub}}=\rho_o gV
\]
so
\[
\frac{V_{\mathrm{sub}}}{V}=\frac{\rho_o}{\rho_f}=\frac{600}{1000}=0.60
\]
\(60\%\) of the volume is submerged.

questions.prompt: A floating block has mass \(1.8\,\mathrm{kg}\). Find the volume of water it displaces.
questions.answer:
For floating equilibrium, the displaced water mass equals the block mass:
\[
\rho_w V_{\mathrm{disp}}=m
\]
\[
V_{\mathrm{disp}}=\frac{1.8}{1000}=1.8\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3}
\]

questions.prompt: An object floats in freshwater with \(72\%\) of its volume submerged. Find its average density.
questions.answer:
For a floating object,
\[
\frac{V_{\mathrm{sub}}}{V}=\frac{\rho_o}{\rho_f}
\]
so
\[
\rho_o=(0.72)(1000)=720\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}
\]

questions.prompt: The same fully submerged object is placed first in water and then in a liquid of density \(1260\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\). Compare the buoyant forces.
questions.answer:
For the same fully submerged object, \(V_{\mathrm{disp}}\) is the same, so
\[
\frac{F_{B,\mathrm{liquid}}}{F_{B,\mathrm{water}}}
=\frac{\rho_{\mathrm{liquid}}}{\rho_{\mathrm{water}}}
=\frac{1260}{1000}=1.26
\]
The denser liquid gives \(1.26\) times the buoyant force in water.

questions.prompt: A solid object has volume \(1.2\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3}\) and density \(2700\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\). Find its apparent weight while fully submerged in water.
questions.answer:
The true weight is
\[
W=\rho_oVg=(2700)(1.2\times10^{-3})(9.8)=31.8\,\mathrm{N}
\]
The buoyant force is
\[
F_B=(1000)(9.8)(1.2\times10^{-3})=11.8\,\mathrm{N}
\]
The apparent weight is
\[
W_{\mathrm{app}}=W-F_B=20.0\,\mathrm{N}
\]

questions.prompt: An object weighs \(18\,\mathrm{N}\) in air and \(11\,\mathrm{N}\) when fully submerged in water. Find its volume and average density.
questions.answer:
The loss of apparent weight is the buoyant force:
\[
F_B=18-11=7\,\mathrm{N}
\]
Thus
\[
V=\frac{7}{(1000)(9.8)}=7.14\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m^3}
\]
The mass is \(m=W/g=18/9.8=1.84\,\mathrm{kg}\), so
\[
\rho=\frac{1.84}{7.14\times10^{-4}}=2.6\times10^3\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}
\]

questions.prompt: A cube of side \(0.20\,\mathrm{m}\) and density \(750\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\) floats upright in water. Find the submerged height.
questions.answer:
The submerged fraction is
\[
\frac{V_{\mathrm{sub}}}{V}=\frac{750}{1000}=0.75
\]
For an upright cube, height fraction equals volume fraction:
\[
h_{\mathrm{sub}}=0.75(0.20)=0.15\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: A vertical floating cylinder has cross-sectional area \(0.030\,\mathrm{m^2}\) and mass \(18\,\mathrm{kg}\). Find its submerged depth in water.
questions.answer:
For floating equilibrium,
\[
\rho_wgAh=mg
\]
so
\[
h=\frac{m}{\rho_wA}=\frac{18}{(1000)(0.030)}=0.60\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: A sealed raft has volume \(0.60\,\mathrm{m^3}\) and mass \(180\,\mathrm{kg}\). Find the maximum extra mass it can carry in water before it is just fully submerged.
questions.answer:
At the just-fully-submerged point, the maximum supported total mass is the displaced water mass:
\[
m_{\mathrm{total,max}}=\rho_wV=(1000)(0.60)=600\,\mathrm{kg}
\]
The extra mass is
\[
m_{\mathrm{extra,max}}=600-180=420\,\mathrm{kg}
\]

questions.prompt: A fully submerged object has volume \(1.0\times10^{-2}\,\mathrm{m^3}\) and weight \(70\,\mathrm{N}\). It is tethered underwater in water. Find the tether force and its direction on the object.
questions.answer:
The buoyant force is
\[
F_B=(1000)(9.8)(1.0\times10^{-2})=98\,\mathrm{N}
\]
Since \(F_B>W\), the object would rise unless the tether pulls downward. Equilibrium gives
\[
F_B-W-T=0
\]
\[
T=98-70=28\,\mathrm{N}
\]
The tether force on the object is downward.

questions.prompt: A solid of volume \(4.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3}\) and density \(1200\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\) is held fully submerged in oil of density \(850\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\). Find the string tension needed for equilibrium and its direction on the solid.
questions.answer:
The weight is
\[
W=\rho_oVg=(1200)(4.0\times10^{-3})(9.8)=47.0\,\mathrm{N}
\]
The buoyant force is
\[
F_B=(850)(4.0\times10^{-3})(9.8)=33.3\,\mathrm{N}
\]
Since the solid is denser than the oil, the string must pull upward:
\[
T=W-F_B=13.7\,\mathrm{N}
\]

questions.prompt: A uniform block of density \(900\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\) floats at the interface between oil \((800\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}})\) above and water \((1000\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}})\) below. If the block has vertical height \(H\), find the fraction of its height in water.
questions.answer:
Let \(x\) be the height of the block in water. The rest, \(H-x\), is in oil. With common cross-sectional area \(A\),
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{block}}gAH=\rho_wgAx+\rho_ogA(H-x)
\]
Cancel \(gA\):
\[
900H=1000x+800(H-x)
\]
\[
100H=200x
\]
\[
\frac{x}{H}=0.50
\]
Half the height is in water and half is in oil.

questions.prompt: A hydrometer of mass \(0.020\,\mathrm{kg}\) has a narrow vertical stem of cross-sectional area \(1.0\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m^2}\). It floats first in water and then in a liquid of density \(800\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\). Find how much farther the stem sinks in the lower-density liquid.
questions.answer:
Floating requires
\[
V_{\mathrm{disp}}=\frac{m}{\rho_f}
\]
In water,
\[
V_w=\frac{0.020}{1000}=2.0\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m^3}
\]
In the lower-density liquid,
\[
V_l=\frac{0.020}{800}=2.5\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m^3}
\]
The extra displaced volume is \(5.0\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m^3}\). With stem area \(A\),
\[
\Delta h=\frac{\Delta V}{A}=\frac{5.0\times10^{-6}}{1.0\times10^{-4}}=0.050\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: A composite floating body is made from foam of volume \(0.030\,\mathrm{m^3}\) and density \(120\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\), plus a metal insert of volume \(0.0020\,\mathrm{m^3}\) and density \(7800\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\). Determine whether it floats in water and, if so, what fraction of its total volume is submerged.
questions.answer:
The total mass is
\[
m=(120)(0.030)+(7800)(0.0020)=3.6+15.6=19.2\,\mathrm{kg}
\]
The total volume is
\[
V=0.030+0.0020=0.032\,\mathrm{m^3}
\]
If fully submerged, the maximum displaced water mass is \(32\,\mathrm{kg}\), greater than \(19.2\,\mathrm{kg}\), so the body floats.
The displaced volume is
\[
V_{\mathrm{sub}}=\frac{m}{\rho_w}=\frac{19.2}{1000}=0.0192\,\mathrm{m^3}
\]
so the submerged fraction is
\[
\frac{0.0192}{0.032}=0.60
\]

questions.prompt: A wooden float of volume \(0.040\,\mathrm{m^3}\) and density \(550\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\) has a dense metal piece of density \(7800\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\) attached to it. Derive and calculate the maximum metal volume before the combination just sinks in water.
questions.answer:
At the sinking threshold, the combination is just fully submerged:
\[
\rho_w(V_w+V_m)=\rho_{\mathrm{wood}}V_w+\rho_mV_m
\]
Rearrange:
\[
(\rho_w-\rho_{\mathrm{wood}})V_w=(\rho_m-\rho_w)V_m
\]
\[
V_m=\frac{\rho_w-\rho_{\mathrm{wood}}}{\rho_m-\rho_w}V_w
\]
Numerically,
\[
V_m=\frac{1000-550}{7800-1000}(0.040)=2.65\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3}
\]

questions.prompt: A vertical cylinder of cross-sectional area \(A\) and height \(H\) is fully submerged from depth \(y=a\) to \(y=a+H\) in a fluid with density \(\rho(y)=\rho_0(1+\beta y)\). Derive the buoyant force.
questions.answer:
The buoyant force equals the weight of the displaced fluid. For a vertical slice, \(dV=A\,dy\):
\[
F_B=g\int_a^{a+H}\rho(y)A\,dy
\]
\[
F_B=\rho_0gA\int_a^{a+H}(1+\beta y)\,dy
\]
\[
F_B=\rho_0gA\left[H+\beta\left(aH+\frac{H^2}{2}\right)\right]
\]
The force is upward. The dependence on \(a\) appears because the fluid density changes with depth.

questions.prompt: A uniform object floats in a liquid inside an elevator accelerating upward with acceleration \(a\). Using an effective gravitational field \(g+a\), show whether the submerged fraction changes compared with the elevator at rest. State the assumptions.
questions.answer:
In the accelerating elevator model, replace \(g\) by \(g+a\) for both the object's effective weight and the buoyant force.
Floating equilibrium gives
\[
\rho_f(g+a)V_{\mathrm{sub}}=\rho_o(g+a)V
\]
Cancel \(g+a\):
\[
\frac{V_{\mathrm{sub}}}{V}=\frac{\rho_o}{\rho_f}
\]
The submerged fraction is unchanged. This assumes the fluid is at rest relative to the elevator, densities are unchanged, and the effective-gravity model is valid throughout the container.
